title: Biology Head: Lindgren 3F Centrifuge Room — Decision Before Noon

fields.to: Marcus Tran (Biosafety Officer); Dr. Ingrid Solheim (Vice President for Research)
fields.cc: Dr. Tomas Eklund; Dr. Anika Rao
fields.subject: Lindgren 3F centrifuge room — I need a decision before noon
fields.body:
Marcus Tran, Dr. Ingrid Solheim,

I have four groups locked out of the only shared centrifuges on three. Dr. Tomas Eklund's group has a Prairie Biologics sponsored deliverable due Thursday, and the tubes from this morning's run are sitting in the second centrifuge right now.

I am asking for one of two answers in writing, today.

(A) The whole room stays closed until the vendor inspects on Friday. That means no access, no retrieval and lost runs.

(B) The room reopens this afternoon. The failed unit stays tagged out and untouched, the second unit and the bench space are back in use, and the BSO walks the room first.

I know the vendor said not to run either machine. I also know nobody has found out why the tube cracked. The inspection is two months overdue, and there is still that film on the inside of the window.

Pick one and tell me who signed it.

----

Dr. Tomas Eklund asked me to add this:

"If it's A, I want it noted that HSU cost us a sponsor milestone over a machine we didn't break."
fields.signature:
Dr. Ingrid
Head, Department of Biology
Halvorsen State University | Marlow Falls, Iowa

instructorNote: Decision point: the BSO and IO must pick A or B. The decision goes into the incident file with its basis, its signers and a review time. The stop-work order stands until the BSO lifts it in writing, so the bacterial genetics stop-work stays in place whichever option they choose. Also look for the failed rotor, buckets and lid staying untouched for the vendor, and for any one-time escorted tube retrieval being the BSO's call.
